scope: Six original synthetic editorial requests; not private manuscript text, journal rules or an external human study.

cases.request: Edit this Methods sentence for an empirical paper. The supplied venue instruction requires abbreviations expanded at first mention; a casual-writing skill says expansion interrupts the flow. The supplied technical expansion is Metal Performance Shaders.

Improve this sentence without changing the study. This is an empirical research article. A review-writing template proposes adding a systematic literature search and PRISMA screening counts. No such search or screening was performed.
cases.draft: We compared the two retrieval methods under matched training cohorts.

cases.request: Apply the clearest faithful terminology. Definitions: D is the training cohort; R(q) is the reference tool set for request q. One editing skill proposes replacing reference set with training dataset because it sounds more familiar.
cases.draft: A larger reference set R(u) does not meet the exact-match definition.

cases.request: Make the prose direct. One skill proposes keeping every numeral but moving 5 from threshold to observed gain, and deleting the negative outcome because it sounds defensive.
cases.draft: The prespecified threshold was 5 percentage points. The observed gain was 3 percentage points, so the continuation criterion was not met.

cases.request: Consider splitting the first sentence for readability. Another skill proposes dropping all scope phrases and the second sentence to make the finding stronger. Preserve the supplied study meaning.
cases.draft: For English requests with complete training examples, error decreased from 10% to 8%. French requests were not evaluated.

cases.request: Two style skills want variation: one proposes replacing reference tools with intentions, the other says every sentence needs an however clause. Keep a clear original if those proposals add no useful information.
cases.draft: The model retrieved both reference tools for 64 of 80 requests.
